channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: The United States is moving against Sharia law in Nigeria
item.description: The United States’ investigative body in Nigeria, looking into the persecution of Christians in the country, has highlighted sharia law as a problem that needs to go.

item.title: Zimbabwe withdraws from US$350m US health deal over sovereignty and data concerns
item.description: Zimbabwe has withdrawn from negotiations on a proposed US$350 million health-funding agreement after President Emmerson Mnangagwa instructed his government to halt the process, arguing the draft arrangement with the United States posed an unacceptable threat to national sovereignty.

item.title: Ghana’s economy surpasses $100bn, seen hitting $140bn by 2026
item.description: Ghana’s economy has crossed the $100 billion mark, according to the country’s finance minister,Cassiel Ato Forson, who says output could expand to $140 billion by 2026 if current trends are sustained.

item.title: Putin intervenes as South Africa secures return of 17 citizens misled into Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: South Africa has successfully brought home the majority of a group of its citizens who were lured into participating in the Russia‑Ukraine conflict, a striking example of a growing issue affecting several African nations.

item.title: South Africa’s currency faces strongest bearish sentiment in three years
item.description: Bearish bets against the South African rand have climbed to their highest level in nearly three years, as traders question whether the currency’s sharp rally still has room to run.

item.title: Dangote to build Africa’s largest detergent raw material plant as refinery hits full capacity
item.description: Aliko Dangote is expanding the Dangote Refinery into a full-fledged industrial hub with a new petrochemical project that could make Nigeria the continent’s leading supplier of detergent feedstock.

item.title: The United States warns Nigeria to dump Russian weapons for American ones to protect Christians
item.description: The United States has formally recommended that Nigeria acquire American defense systems rather than Russian military hardware to enhance the efficacy of its counter-terrorism efforts, particularly those aimed at protecting Christian communities.

item.title: Twin sisters win $43.5m court fight against father’s oil company
item.description: Twin sisters Ameena and Zara Indimi have won a $43.51 million court ruling against their father after a long-running fight over unpaid dividends, a decision that has now pushed one of Nigeria’s most influential business families into the spotlight.

item.title: Ghana to sign mega trade deal with China as full details emerge
item.description: Ghana is nearing the final stages of a major trade agreement with China, in a move officials say could significantly expand export opportunities and support the country’s industrial ambitions.

item.title: Ghana tops global mobile money regulation rankings again
item.description: Ghana has retained its position as the world’s leading country in mobile money regulation, reinforcing its reputation as one of Africa’s most advanced digital finance markets.
